title: Jia-Qi Zheng
text:
Our Lab was founded in September 2024 by Prof. Jia-qi Zheng. It is affiliated with the Guangdong Institute of Smart Education at Jinan University (JNU). We specialize in international large-scale educational assessment studies, such as PISA, TIMSS, and PIRLS. By leveraging cutting-edge technologies, including deep learning, machine learning, and explainable artificial intelligence. We aim to investigate key factors influencing students’ cognitive and non-cognitive competencies, behavioral patterns, as well as crucial topics regarding affective computing, which covers emotion recognition, reasoning, and generation.
Our lab is a multidisciplinary team composed of researchers from educational technology, computer science, and sociology. Currently, our work focuses on topics including students’ academic resilience, self-efficacy, well-being, subject-specific competencies, and emotion-related processes in learning contexts.
We warmly welcome interdisciplinary collaboration. For further information or to discuss potential collaborations, please feel free to contact Prof. Jia-qi Zheng at jqzheng@jnu.edu.cn.

title: resources
text: It’s finally time for an upgraded notebook! I’ve been Slacking myself (and subsequently burying) links to resources for far too long, so my favorites will now live here.

title: resources
text:
learning materials

Ever feel like you need a pick-me-up while learning stats or a new R tool? Look no further than Allison Horst’s Data Science Illustrations, featuring the cutest and most educational fuzzy monsters you’ll ever see!
Mastering Shiny, by Hadley Wickham
Happy Git and GitHub for the useR, by Jenny Bryan
R for Data Science, by Hadley Wickham
Hitchhiker’s Guide to Python, by Kenneth Reitz & Tanya Schlusser
Data wrangling essentials: comparisons in JavaScript, Python, SQL, R, and Excel, by Allison Horst & Paul Buffa
W3Schools, particularly for their HTML & CSS tutorials

title: resources
text:
data viz

from Data to Viz, a choose-your-adventure-type experience for creating your best data visualizations
Fundamentals of Data Visualization, by Claus O. Wilke
The Sessions College Color Calculator, for creating color palettes
Beautifully Annotated: Enhancing your ggplots with Text, by Cara Thompson, a seriously wonderful talk on using annotations in your ggplots

title: resources
text:
r tools

free icons from fontawesome + the {fontawesome} R package for infusing your slides, website, RMarkdowns/Quarto Markdowns, and more with an extra splash of fun

title: resources
text:
reporting & presentations

Quarto is all the rage these days (and by these days, I mean post-March 2022). Download and find some great tutorials here to get started
Meet xaringan: Making slides in R Markdown, by Allison Hill
Sharing Your xaringan Slides, by Garrick Aden-Buie

title: resources
text:
data science communities
While these groups are primarily based in SoCal/Santa Barbara, there are tons of awesome groups like these all over the world. Google around to see what’s near you!

R-Ladies Santa Barbara and R-Ladies Global, which work to promote gender diversity in the R community
EcoDataScience, an environmental data science study group at UCSB

Southern California R Users, an alliance of R user groups in Southern California

Santa Barbara Women in STEM, while not specifically data science-focused, this group holds some really great career and networking events, panels, flash talks, and more

title: resources
text:
web accessibility

The A11Y Project is a community-driven effort to make digital content more accessible. I still have a long way to go in making my own website WCAG compliant – the A11Y Project not only has a ton of great blog posts, but also WCAG compliance checklist that I will definitely be returning to over and over again.
Coblis, a color blindness simulator – just upload a file and view your color palettes as they would appear under different types of color deficiencies

text:
The 12th Summer School on Data Science and Engineering



Abstract
Keynote speaker at the 12th Summer School on Data Science and Engineering held at East China Normal University in Shanghai in July 2025. This prestigious summer school brought together researchers, students, and professionals in the field of data science and engineering to share knowledge, discuss latest developments, and foster collaborative learning in this rapidly evolving discipline.


Event Details

Date: July 2025
Location: East China Normal University, Shanghai
Event: the 12th Summer School on Data Science and Engineering
Role: Keynote Speaker



Audience
This summer school was designed for graduate students, researchers, and professionals interested in data science and engineering to engage in advanced training, lectures, and networking with leading experts in the field.
